Definition: from a presumed derivative of G4429 (and thus akin to G4422); to frighten:--terrify.
BiblicalUsage: Pturo means to frighten, to terrify. It appears once, and Paul turns it into a command: in nothing terrified by your adversaries, which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe my fearlessness is itself a witness: the adversary reads it as his own ruin and my salvation, because only God could make a man unafraid.
